rows.text: The commander is a two-spells-a-turn engine with a bill attached. Every spell you cast hands an opponent a card — but it also grows a creature, gives it flying, and the SECOND resolution each turn draws you two. So the deck is built almost entirely out of cheap creatures and flash creatures, cast two at a time, every turn including everyone else's. The board goes wide, then goes airborne.

guide.title: The commander and the second-spell rule

rows.name: Ms. Bumbleflower
rows.text: cast a spell: an opponent draws, one of your creatures gets a permanent +1/+1 counter and temporary flying. Cast a second one the same turn and you draw two. Count to two every turn — that is the whole deck.

rows.name: Ledger Shredder
rows.text: connives on EVERY player's second spell, not just yours. The cards you are handing out with Bumbleflower push opponents into their own second spell, which turns her downside into your card selection.

rows.name: Harvestrite Host
rows.text: the same "second time this turn" clause on Rabbit enters. Two Rabbits in a turn is a card, and half the creature base is a Rabbit.

rows.name: Pollywog Prodigy
rows.text: draws off their cheap noncreature spells. Evolve keeps its power climbing, which widens what it draws from.

rows.name: Aerial Extortionist
rows.text: exiles a nonland permanent on entry and again on every hit, and draws whenever anyone casts from exile or a graveyard.

rows.name: Twenty-Toed Toad
rows.text: the sleeper win condition. It grows and draws every time you attack with two creatures, and it wins outright at twenty counters or twenty cards in hand — and Curiosity Crafter removes your maximum hand size to get there.

guide.title: Flash: casting your second spell on their turn

rows.name: Aven Interrupter
rows.text: flash, flies, exiles a spell on the stack outright, and taxes everything they try to cast back out of exile or the graveyard afterwards.

rows.name: Aven Mindcensor
rows.text: flash him in response to the fetch or the tutor. Four cards deep instead of a library.

rows.name: Whitemane Lion
rows.text: two mana at instant speed that rebuys any enter-the-battlefield creature and counts as a spell.

rows.name: Kutzil's Flanker
rows.text: flash, and all three modes are live — counters, life and scry, or exiling a graveyard deck's yard at the worst moment for them.

rows.name: Plumecreed Escort
rows.text: flash flier that saves your commander from removal.

rows.name: Skycoach Conductor
rows.text: flash flier that enters prepared, so it is two spells in one card — the creature now and a free blink later.

rows.name: Enduring Curiosity
rows.text: flash it in before combat and every connecting creature draws. It comes back as an enchantment when it dies, so removal does not really answer it.

rows.name: Studious First-Year
rows.text: a one-mana body that is also a Rampant Growth later, again splitting one card into two spells.

rows.name: Emeritus of Truce
rows.text: a body now and a Swords to Plowshares held in reserve, which is the cleanest removal in the colours.

guide.title: Counters, and the payoff for having them

rows.name: Good-Fortune Unicorn
rows.text: a +1/+1 counter on every creature that enters. With this out, every token maker is also an anthem.

rows.name: Emiel the Blessed
rows.text: counters on entry for {G/W}, and a repeatable blink for every enter-the-battlefield creature in the deck. It is also the engine half of the Preston loop below.

rows.name: Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar
rows.text: opponents cannot cast spells during your turn — a Grand Abolisher on a body — and draws whenever creatures whose power exceeds their BASE power connect. Bumbleflower and the Unicorn are constantly making that true.

rows.name: Sovereign Okinec Ahau
rows.text: the same "bigger than base" trigger pointed at combat, snowballing counters onto the whole attack.

rows.name: Finneas, Ace Archer
rows.text: counters on every token and every Rabbit each attack, plus a card once the board reaches ten power. Two mana.

rows.name: Gavony Township
rows.text: the mana sink that keeps doing it when your hand is empty.

rows.name: Rigo, Streetwise Mentor
rows.text: draws for attacking with the small creatures the deck makes anyway, and enters with a shield counter so removal costs them two cards.

rows.name: Warren Warleader
rows.text: Offspring makes two of it, and every attack is either another attacking Rabbit or a team pump.

rows.name: Jacked Rabbit
rows.text: an X-cost body that makes tokens equal to its power on every attack.

rows.name: Brimaz, King of Oreskos
rows.text: a token when it attacks AND a token when it blocks, which makes it the best three-drop to hold the fort with.

rows.name: Ocelot Pride
rows.text: a Cat every end step you gained life, doubled once you have the city's blessing. Hinterland Sanctifier makes that condition true on every creature you play.

rows.name: Hinterland Sanctifier
rows.text: one life per creature entering. It looks like filler; it is what turns Ocelot Pride on every single turn and what gets Felidar Sovereign to forty.

rows.name: Preston, the Vanisher
rows.text: copies every nontoken creature that arrives WITHOUT being cast — so every Emiel blink, every Broodmoth return, every Jackdaw Savior reanimation makes an extra Illusion. Five Illusions exile any nonland permanent, which is this deck's answer to a problem it cannot attack.

rows.name: Prava of the Steel Legion
rows.text: your tokens are +1/+4 on your turn, which means the 1/1s attack as 2/5s and still survive blocking.

rows.name: Pollen-Shield Hare
rows.text: a permanent anthem for tokens on one half and a game-ending pump on the other.

rows.name: Luminous Broodmoth
rows.text: your ground creatures come back with flying when they die. Combined with a table full of ground blockers, this is how the stall breaks — and it is permanent, unlike Bumbleflower's until-end-of-turn flying.

rows.name: Jackdaw Savior
rows.text: every flier that dies reanimates something cheaper. With Broodmoth turning your dead ground creatures into fliers, the two of them recur each other all game.

rows.name: Curiosity Crafter
rows.text: a card for every token that connects, and no maximum hand size for the Toad plan.

rows.name: Mr. Foxglove
rows.text: draws you back up to whichever opponent is hoarding cards — which, since Bumbleflower has been feeding them, is usually a lot — or puts a creature down for free.

rows.name: Skyhunter Strike Force
rows.text: melee for the whole team while you control your commander, so a four-player attack is a +3/+3 anthem.

rows.name: Jazal Goldmane
rows.text: the mana sink that ends the game once the board is wide.

rows.name: Bast, Panther Goddess
rows.text: indestructible, and every attack pumps one creature by the size of your board.

rows.name: Enduring Vitality
rows.text: every creature taps for any colour. On a wide board this is more mana than any rock in the format, and it comes back as an enchantment when it dies.

rows.name: Arbor Adherent
rows.text: taps for X equal to the greatest toughness among your OTHER creatures — Ms. Bumbleflower alone makes that five.

rows.name: Gaea's Cradle
rows.text: the same idea from the mana base.

rows.name: Three Tree City
rows.text: name Rabbit or Cat and it is a second Cradle.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: turn-one acceleration into the two-spell turns the commander wants.

rows.name: Gilded Goose
rows.text: mana now, and the Food is Thornvault Forager's fuel later.

rows.name: Poison Dart Frog
rows.text: fixes, and gives itself deathtouch to hold the ground while you set up.

rows.name: Traveling Chocobo
rows.text: doubles every land and Bird enters trigger you control, and this deck plays eleven Birds. Cast Clifftop Lookout with it out and you get two lands.

rows.name: Selfless Savior
rows.text: one mana, saves the commander from the first removal spell.

rows.name: Dauntless Escort
rows.text: saves the whole board from the first wrath.

rows.name: Spore Frog
rows.text: fogs the alpha strike that would otherwise kill you before the board is set.

rows.name: Prowling Serpopard
rows.text: your creature spells cannot be countered, and it cannot be countered itself.

rows.name: Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd
rows.text: flickers their blocker, their equipment or their enchantment out of the way each attack, and grows doing it.

rows.name: Qasali Pridemage
rows.text: artifact and enchantment removal stapled to a two-drop.

rows.name: Curious Farm Animals
rows.text: the same, on a one-drop that gains you three life for Felidar and Ocelot Pride.

rows.name: Felidar Sovereign
rows.text: forty life is not a stretch in a deck with Hinterland Sanctifier, three lifelinkers and a board that gains on every creature. Win at your upkeep.

rows.name: Twenty-Toed Toad
rows.text: twenty cards in hand with Curiosity Crafter out, or twenty counters from repeated two-creature attacks.
Both are real, but neither is the plan. The plan is a wide board with counters on it that Ms. Bumbleflower makes fly for a turn.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep cheap. Two one- or two-drops and three lands beats a hand with a five-drop in it, because the commander only pays out when you can deploy twice in a turn.

rows.name: Ms. Bumbleflower
rows.text: four mana, and she is not urgent. Every spell she sees hands an opponent a card, so casting her on an empty board with nothing to follow up is pure charity — get bodies down first, then cast her into a turn where you can immediately follow with a one-drop.
Hold one flash creature whenever you can. It makes your second spell on THEIR turn, which is a free two cards you would not otherwise get.

rows.name: Preston, the Vanisher
rows.text: only good after Emiel, Broodmoth or Jackdaw Savior. On its own it does very little; sequenced behind any of them it takes over the game.
